reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes MTI mirror trading with specific high-income claims, including $15,000 per day, $330,000 per month, and projected binary bonuses tied to time periods and team-member counts. It links financial freedom and potential bonuses to sharing the business, recruiting, and growing a team, and directs viewers to join MTI or contact the sender for more information. Non-guarantee and trading-results disclaimers are included, while the available video evidence does not establish actual earnings, required enrollment payments, completed transactions, or subsequent outcomes.

citations.quote: MTI Mirror Trading MAKE $12,928 Per Month
The Highly Effective people will generally share the business with someone every day. They will recruit
The more effort you are able to put into growing your business the quicker you will achieve financial freedom.
potential binary bonus per week US$3232
It must be noted that all bonuses are dependent on trading results.

opening.argument: Judge, the headline's monthly figure should be read alongside the presentation's express limits, not as a promised payout. The speaker says the ideas may not work for every viewer, calls the projections history-based, and makes bonuses dependent on trading results. The presentation also warns viewers not to count on spillover before it occurs. Those qualifications matter when deciding whether this is a deceptive earnings solicitation: the video describes possibilities while explicitly withholding a guarantee.

citations.quote: MTI Mirror Trading MAKE $12,928 Per Month
We can't guarantee that the ideas shown in this video will work for you.
All projections made in this video are based on current history. It must be noted that all bonuses are dependent on trading results.
But don't count on spillover until it actually occurs.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited title and binary-bonus figure are attention-grabbing, but neither establishes that a viewer is promised that income. The cited claim about financial freedom describes what greater effort might achieve; it does not erase the explicit qualification that bonuses depend on trading results. Recruitment is discussed, but the prosecution's quotes do not show that the stated figures are guaranteed payments for recruiting.

citations.quote: It must be noted that all bonuses are dependent on trading results.
potential binary bonus per week US$3232

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A disclaimer does not change the pitch's mechanism. The presentation pairs a projected $3,232 weekly binary bonus with 2,309 team members in the weaker leg, and tells viewers that growing their team leads toward financial freedom. Even spillover is defined as someone above placing a person in the viewer's leg. The defense's quotes qualify the outcomes, but they do not make recruitment and downline growth incidental to the earnings appeal.

citations.quote: The more effort you are able to put into growing your business the quicker you will achieve financial freedom.
Spillover happens when your sponsor or someone in the team above you places someone in the leg beneath you.

opening.argument: Judge, much of the video functions as an operational lesson: it compares a steady track with a fast track, walks through modeled recruiting results, and points viewers to separate material on how binary bonuses are calculated. It also identifies educational videos and support materials for building the business. That makes the income tables intelligible as worked projections for understanding a business plan, rather than proof that the viewer will receive the displayed amounts.

citations.quote: We will show you a steady track and then the fast track approach
On this table you can see the types of recruiting results each of these types of people will get
more information on how the Bionary Bonuses are calculated, please refer to the Bionary Bonus videos
Merit Training International provides you with educational videos and other support materials to assist you in building your business.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the lesson discusses recruiting and projected bonuses. But those subjects are also what the tables purport to explain: types of participants, their recruiting assumptions, and resulting examples. The cited $3,232 is expressly a potential weekly bonus, not evidence that anyone receives it. Likewise, an invitation to ask the sender questions does not itself establish an enrollment or payment transaction.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The instructional format serves the promotion rather than separating it from the earnings pitch. The video models recruits by participant type, links growing a team to financial freedom, and supplies a way to join MTI. Explaining how the projected bonuses are calculated does not alter the central appeal: building a recruitment network is presented as a path to substantial income.

opening.argument: Judge, the observed material is a promotion of a business, but it does not show a completed transaction or establish that a viewer must pay to participate. It describes sharing the business, using social media, gathering leads, and working with a sponsor, all recognizable business-development activities. The speaker also says bonuses depend on trading results, which complicates the inference that recruitment alone mechanically pays the advertised amounts. Treat the recruitment projections as claims requiring scrutiny, not as proof of an unshown payment or inevitable outcome.

Funnel systems are also effective for gathering leads if you are prepared to pay for the promotion of these on Facebook.
It must be noted that all bonuses are dependent on trading results.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's evidence supports concern about the income pitch, but it stops short of showing a required viewer deposit, a completed payment, or actual bonus disbursement. Even the cited weekly amount is described as potential. Those missing elements matter when deciding how much the video itself proves about a fraudulent transaction, as distinct from an aggressive business promotion.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A completed payment is not needed to assess what the video promotes. It directs viewers to join MTI, models how frequently participants share the plan and recruit, and associates team size with projected binary bonuses. The defense correctly notes that trading results qualify bonuses, but that does not remove the depicted tiered recruitment structure from the financial pitch.
